plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, what is the minimum number of designated partners required to be individuals for a valid LLP incorporation?
options: At least one
At least two
At least three
At least four
plain.explanation: Section 7 of the LLP Act, 2008 mandates that every LLP must have at least two designated partners who are individuals, and at least one of them must be a resident in India. Therefore, the minimum number of designated partners is two.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following bodies corporate is specifically competent to be a partner in a Limited Liability Partnership as per the LLP Act, 2008?
options: A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)
A Foreign Limited Liability Partnership
A sole proprietorship firm
An unregistered association of persons
plain.explanation: Section 2(1)(d) defines a body corporate to include a company, an LLP, a limited liability partnership incorporated outside India, but excludes a corporation not incorporated under any law and any other entity notified by the Central Government. A foreign LLP is a body corporate and can be a partner.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the consequence if the number of partners in an LLP is reduced below two for a continuous period of more than six months?
options: The LLP is automatically dissolved
The remaining partner becomes personally liable for all liabilities of the LLP incurred during that period
The Registrar of Companies converts the LLP into a partnership firm
The LLP is penalized with a fine up to Rs. 10,000 only
plain.explanation: Under Section 6 of the LLP Act, 2008, if at any time the number of partners of an LLP is reduced below two and the LLP carries on business for more than six months while the number is so reduced, the person, who is the only partner of the LLP during the time that it so carries on business after those six months, is liable personally for the obligations of the LLP incurred during that period.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Within how many days of incorporation must the Limited Liability Partnership Agreement be filed with the Registrar in Form 3?
options: 15 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
plain.explanation: As per Section 23(2) read with Rule 21 of the LLP Rules, 2009, information concerning the LLP agreement signed at the time of incorporation, or any changes made therein, must be filed with the Registrar in Form 3 within 30 days of incorporation or change.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a minor be admitted as a partner or designated partner in a Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008?
options: Yes, as both a partner and a designated partner
Yes, as a partner only with the consent of all partners
No, a minor cannot be admitted as a partner or designated partner, nor can they hold any beneficial interest in the LLP
Yes, through a natural guardian
plain.explanation: Under the LLP Act, 2008, individuals eligible to be partners must have contractual capacity. A minor lacks capacity to contract, and unlike partnership law under the Partnership Act, 1932, a minor cannot be admitted to the benefits of an LLP nor become a partner or designated partner.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the primary document required for incorporating a Limited Liability Partnership, which incorporates the application for reservation of name, incorporation, and allotment of DIN?
options: Form FiLLiP (Form for incorporation of Limited Liability Partnership)
Form INC-32 (SPICe)
Form LLP-1
Form RUN-LLP
plain.explanation: Rule 16 of the LLP Rules, 2009 prescribes Form FiLLiP (Form for incorporation of Limited Liability Partnership) for incorporating an LLP, replacing the earlier separate name reservation and incorporation steps.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under the LLP Act, 2008, what is the extent of liability of a partner for the wrongful act or omission of another partner?
options: Joint and several liability for all debts of the LLP
Unlimited personal liability for acts of all partners
No personal liability, except for their own wrongful act or omission
Liability limited to their unpaid capital contribution only
plain.explanation: Section 28(2) of the LLP Act states that an LLP is not bound by anything done by a partner in dealing with a person if the partner has no authority to act for the LLP and the person knows that. Furthermore, a partner is not personally liable, directly or indirectly, for an obligation solely by reason of being a partner of the LLP, protecting them from another partner's wrongful acts unless they participated in it.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What constitutes a 'resident in India' for the purpose of being a designated partner under Section 7 of the LLP Act, 2008?
options: A person who has stayed in India for not less than 120 days during the financial year
A person who has stayed in India for not less than 182 days during the immediately preceding one financial year
An Indian citizen regardless of their residential status
Any person holding an Indian passport
plain.explanation: Section 7(1) explanation specifies that for the purposes of this section, 'resident in India' means a person who has stayed in India for a period of not less than 182 days during the immediately preceding one financial year.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: In the absence of an agreement between the partners regarding mutual rights and duties, what shall govern the relationship of the partners and the LLP?
options: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 provisions
The Companies Act, 2013 schedules
First Schedule to the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008
Rules framed by the Central Government on a case-by-case basis
plain.explanation: Section 23(4) of the LLP Act, 2008 provides that in the absence of agreement as to any matter, the mutual rights and duties of the partners and the mutual rights and duties of the LLP and its partners shall be determined by the provisions relating to that matter as are set out in the First Schedule.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which authority is empowered to order the investigation of the affairs of an LLP under the LLP Act, 2008?
options: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
The Central Government
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
The Registrar of Companies directly without government approval
plain.explanation: Section 43 of the LLP Act, 2008 empowers the Central Government to appoint one or more competent inspectors to investigate the affairs of an LLP and to report thereon in such manner as it may direct.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the maximum number of partners permitted in a Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008?
options: 50 partners
100 partners
200 partners
No upper limit
plain.explanation: Unlike companies or traditional partnerships, the LLP Act, 2008 does not prescribe any upper limit on the maximum number of partners that an LLP can have.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: When can an LLP be wound up voluntarily by its partners?
options: At any time by a simple majority of partners
Only when the Tribunal passes an order
In accordance with the LLP agreement or by passing a resolution to wind up voluntarily
Voluntary winding up of an LLP is not permitted under the law
plain.explanation: Section 63 of the LLP Act, 2008 provides that an LLP may be wound up voluntarily if the LLP passes a resolution to wind up voluntarily and the partners have agreed in the LLP agreement or by a separate resolution.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the penalty for carrying on business with an intent to defraud creditors or any other fraudulent purpose under Section 30 of the LLP Act?
options: Imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to Rs. 50,000
Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 5 years and fine which shall not be less than Rs. 50,000 but may extend to Rs. 5 lakhs
Fine only up to Rs. 1 lakh
Automatic disqualification of all partners without fine
plain.explanation: Section 30 deals with fraudulent trading. If an LLP or any of its partners carries on business with intent to defraud creditors or for any fraudulent purpose, every partner who was knowingly a party to it shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term up to 5 years and a fine of Rs. 50,000 to Rs. 5 lakhs.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the name of a Limited Liability Partnership?
options: The name must end with the words 'Limited Liability Partnership' or the acronym 'LLP'.
The name can be identical to an existing company without any restriction.
The name cannot contain any geographical identifier.
The word 'LLP' is optional for service-oriented LLPs.
plain.explanation: Section 15(1) of the LLP Act, 2008 mandates that every limited liability partnership shall have either the words 'limited liability partnership' or the acronym 'LLP' as the last words of its name.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under Section 34 of the LLP Act, 2008, every LLP is required to maintain books of account which must be preserved for how many years from the date on which they are prepared?
options: 3 years
5 years
8 years
10 years
plain.explanation: Rule 24 of the LLP Rules, 2009 read with Section 34 mandates that the books of account of an LLP shall be maintained on cash or accrual basis and according to double entry system of accounting, and shall be preserved for eight years from the date on which they are prepared.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can a corporate body act as a 'designated partner' in a Limited Liability Partnership?
options: Yes, any body corporate can be a designated partner directly.
No, only individuals can be designated partners.
Yes, provided its net worth exceeds Rs. 5 crores.
Yes, through its nominee who must be an individual.
plain.explanation: Section 7(1) states that designated partners must be individuals. If a body corporate is a partner, it may nominate an individual to act as a designated partner through its resolution.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the consequence of registering an LLP under a name which is identical with or too nearly resembles that of an existing partnership firm or LLP?
options: The Central Government can direct the LLP to change its name within a specified period.
The registration is void ab initio.
The partners face immediate imprisonment.
The Registrar automatically liquidates the LLP.
plain.explanation: Section 17 empowers the Central Government to direct an LLP to change its name if it is identical with or too nearly resembles that of any other partnership firm, LLP, or body corporate, or trademark registered under the Trade Marks Act, 1999.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which statement best describes the concept of 'Limited Liability' in an LLP?
options: Partners have no liability whatsoever for any business debts.
The liability of the partners is limited to their agreed contribution to the LLP.
The liability of the LLP is limited, but partners have unlimited personal liability.
Liability is limited only in the event of winding up.
plain.explanation: Section 28 and basic principles of LLP establish that partners are agents of the LLP but not of other partners, and their liability is limited to their agreed contribution to the LLP as specified in the LLP agreement.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Within what period must an LLP file its Annual Return (Form 11) with the Registrar from the close of its financial year?
options: Within 30 days
Within 60 days
Within 90 days
Within 6 months
plain.explanation: Section 35(1) of the LLP Act, 2008 read with Rule 25 requires every LLP to file an annual return with the Registrar in Form 11 within 60 days of closure of its financial year.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the consequence if an LLP fails to file its Statement of Account and Solvency (Form 8) within the prescribed time?
options: The LLP and every designated partner shall be punishable with a fine of Rs. 100 for every day during which the failure continues, subject to a maximum penalty.
The LLP is automatically struck off by the Registrar without notice.
The partners face compulsory imprisonment for 6 months.
All business bank accounts are permanently frozen.
plain.explanation: Section 34(5) specifies that if any LLP fails to comply with the provisions of filing the Statement of Account and Solvency, the LLP and every designated partner of the LLP shall be punishable with a fine of Rs. 100 for each day during which the failure continues, subject to statutory limits.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Can an existing partnership firm convert into a Limited Liability Partnership under the LLP Act, 2008?
options: No, conversion is not permitted under the law.
Yes, provided all partners of the partnership firm agree and the procedure in the Second Schedule is followed.
Yes, only with the prior approval of the Supreme Court.
Yes, but only if the partnership firm was registered under the Companies Act.
plain.explanation: Section 55 read with the Second Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008 permits the conversion of a firm into an LLP by fulfilling specified criteria and filing the necessary application with the Registrar.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the status of an LLP after its incorporation certificate is issued?
options: It becomes a body corporate capable of suing and being sued in its own name, having perpetual succession.
It remains a partnership until the LLP agreement is registered.
It is a trust subject to the Indian Trusts Act.
It requires separate registration as a commercial enterprise with local authorities to gain corporate status.
plain.explanation: Section 3 of the LLP Act, 2008 provides that an LLP is a body corporate formed and incorporated under this Act and is a legal entity separate from its partners, having perpetual succession.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: In the case of a whistleblowing provision under Section 31 of the LLP Act, the Tribunal may reduce or waive the penalty against a partner or employee if they:
options: Resign from the LLP immediately.
Provide useful information during investigation or proceedings leading to conviction or penalty under the Act.
Pay double the penalty amount voluntarily.
Transfer their share to a third party.
plain.explanation: Section 31 provides for relief to partners/employees in certain cases. The Tribunal or Central Government may reduce or waive any penalty against any partner or employee of an LLP if he has given information leading to a conviction or penalty under the Act.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which statement is correct regarding the contribution of partners in a Limited Liability Partnership?
options: Contribution can consist of tangible, intangible property, or other benefits to the LLP.
Contribution must be strictly in cash deposited in a nationalized bank.
Contribution can only be in the form of immovable property.
Partners are not required to make any contribution whatsoever under any circumstance.
plain.explanation: Section 32 states that the contribution of a partner may consist of tangible, movable or immovable or intangible property or other benefit to the LLP, including money, promissory notes, other agreements to contribute cash or property, and contracts for services performed or to be performed.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the timeline for filing a notice of any change in the partners of an LLP with the Registrar after such change takes place?
options: 15 days
30 days
60 days
90 days
plain.explanation: Section 25(1) requires an LLP to ensure that a notice of any change in its partners (with details and consent) is filed with the Registrar within 30 days of such change.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Who is responsible for signing and verifying the Statement of Account and Solvency of an LLP?
options: Any employee designated by the accountant
All partners of the LLP unconditionally
The designated partners of the LLP
The Registrar of Companies
plain.explanation: Section 34(3) stipulates that the Statement of Account and Solvency shall be signed on behalf of the LLP by the designated partners of the LLP.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: When can the Central Government order the winding up of an LLP by the Tribunal?
options: If the LLP acts against the sovereignty and integrity of India or security of the State.
If the LLP fails to make a profit for two consecutive financial years.
If any partner resigns without giving notice.
If the LLP changes its registered office from one state to another.
plain.explanation: Section 64 sets out grounds for winding up by the Tribunal, which includes if the LLP has acted against the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State, or public order.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Which of the following documents forms the constitutional basis for internal governance and management of a Limited Liability Partnership?
options: Memorandum of Association
Articles of Association
Limited Liability Partnership Agreement
Partnership Deed under the Partnership Act
plain.explanation: Section 2(1)(o) and Section 23 define the LLP Agreement as any written agreement between the partners of the LLP or between the LLP and its partners which determines the mutual rights and duties of the partners and their rights and duties in relation to that LLP.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: What is the legal effect of registering a charge created by an LLP under Section 37 of the LLP Act?
options: It makes the charge holder the owner of the LLP's assets.
It provides constructive notice of the charge to any person acquiring an interest in the property or asset charged.
It guarantees repayment of the loan by the Central Government.
It is only an internal record with no legal consequences.
plain.explanation: Registration of charges under the LLP Act operates as constructive notice to third parties who deal with the LLP's assets, ensuring transparency and priority of claims.

plain.subject: Law
plain.prompt: Under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, can an individual cease to be a partner of an LLP by giving notice in writing?
options: No, cessation requires unanimous court order.
Yes, in accordance with the LLP agreement, or by giving 30 days notice to the other partners in the absence of agreement.
Yes, instantly without any notice condition.
No, partners are locked in for the entire life of the LLP.
plain.explanation: Section 24(1) provides that a person may cease to be a partner in accordance with the agreement or, in the absence of agreement, by giving 30 days' notice to the other partners of their intention to resign.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Zenith Advisory LLP was incorporated in Mumbai with three partners: Alpha Corp (a body corporate incorporated in Singapore), Mr. Rohan (an Indian resident), and Ms. Priya (who stays in London and visits India for only 30 days in a financial year). Due to a business dispute, Alpha Corp decides to withdraw its nominee designated partner without appointing a replacement, and Ms. Priya refuses to act as a designated partner. The LLP agreement is silent on the mechanism of appointing designated partners.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Considering the residency requirement under Section 7, which of the partners in Zenith Advisory LLP is qualified to act as a 'resident in India' designated partner?
options: Alpha Corp
Mr. Rohan
Ms. Priya
None of them
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 7 requires at least one designated partner to be resident in India (stay in India for not less than 182 days in the preceding financial year). Mr. Rohan is an Indian resident, whereas Ms. Priya stayed for only 30 days, failing the test.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Alpha Corp withdraws its nominee and no replacement is appointed, what is the minimum number of designated partners Zenith Advisory LLP must maintain under the Act?
options: At least one
At least two
At least three
No minimum is required if total partners are above two
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 7 mandates that every LLP must have at least two designated partners who are individuals. If the number falls below two, the LLP is in default.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Ms. Priya, being a partner who stays abroad for most of the year, be appointed as a designated partner of Zenith Advisory LLP?
options: Yes, provided she holds an Indian PAN card
Yes, as an ordinary designated partner, but she cannot fulfill the resident-in-India requirement
No, individuals who are non-residents can never be designated partners under any circumstance
Yes, if Alpha Corp guarantees her residency
linkedMcqs.explanation: An individual who is a non-resident can be a designated partner, but they will not satisfy the specific requirement that at least one designated partner must be resident in India.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If the LLP fails to maintain the minimum required designated partners for more than 6 months, who faces penal consequences under the LLP Act?
options: Only Alpha Corp as the foreign body corporate
The LLP and every partner/defaulting officer of the LLP
Only the Registrar of Companies
No penalty applies if the total partners exceed two
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 7 and associated penalty provisions state that if an LLP contravenes the provisions relating to designated partners, the LLP and every designated partner/partner in default are punishable with a fine.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: A partnership firm named 'M/s Quick Logistics', consisting of three partners (A, B, and C), decided to convert into a Limited Liability Partnership under the name 'Quick Logistics LLP' following the Second Schedule of the LLP Act, 2008. At the time of conversion, the firm had outstanding unsecured loans from various creditors. The partners did not file Form 3 containing the LLP agreement within 30 days of incorporation, and partner A performed an unauthorized contract beyond his authority, causing loss to a third party who was aware of A's lack of authority.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the legal effect of the conversion of M/s Quick Logistics into Quick Logistics LLP on the property and liabilities of the firm?
options: All property, assets, and liabilities of the firm automatically vest in the LLP without requiring separate conveyancing.
All previous liabilities are extinguished upon conversion.
The firm continues to exist alongside the LLP as a subsidiary.
Only movable assets transfer to the LLP, while liabilities remain with the firm.
linkedMcqs.explanation: As per the Second Schedule of the LLP Act, upon conversion, all tangible and intangible property, assets, rights, privileges, liabilities, and obligations of the firm stand transferred to and vest in the LLP without any further act or deed.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What penalty or consequence follows the failure of Quick Logistics LLP to file Form 3 (LLP Agreement) within 30 days of incorporation?
options: The incorporation certificate is revoked automatically.
The LLP and every partner are liable to a monetary penalty for non-compliance.
The partners face compulsory imprisonment for 3 months.
The LLP agreement becomes permanently void and cannot be registered.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Failing to file Form 3 within the stipulated time attracts monetary penalties for the LLP and its designated partners as specified under Section 23 read with the penal provisions of the Act.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Is Quick Logistics LLP bound by the unauthorized contract entered into by partner A with the third party?
options: Yes, because all partners possess implied authority for all commercial contracts.
No, because the LLP is not bound by anything done by a partner if the partner has no authority and the third party knows that.
Yes, because third parties are never required to check partner authority in an LLP.
No, because only designated partners can bind an LLP.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 28(2) specifies that an LLP is not bound by anything done by a partner in dealing with a person if the partner has no authority to act for the LLP and the person knows that the partner has no authority.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Following the conversion, what happens to the unsecured creditors of the erstwhile partnership firm?
options: They lose their right to claim since the legal entity has changed.
They remain creditors of the newly formed LLP, and their rights are unaffected by the conversion.
They must re-file their claims through court litigation.
Their debts are converted into equity shares of the LLP.
linkedMcqs.explanation: The Second Schedule ensures that all obligations, debts, and liabilities of the firm prior to conversion devolve upon the resulting LLP, preserving the rights of all creditors.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Vanguard Tech Solutions LLP was formed by four software engineers. Due to internal disagreements, Partner X decided to retire from the LLP. The LLP agreement contained a clause specifying a 14-day notice period for voluntary retirement. However, Partner X served a 30-day notice. Simultaneously, the LLP failed to file its Statement of Account and Solvency (Form 8) for the financial year ending March 31, and the Registrar initiated inquiry proceedings.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: How is the retirement of Partner X governed when the LLP agreement prescribes a specific notice period?
options: The agreement provision prevails, making the 14-day notice period applicable.
The statutory default period of 30 days under the Act overrides the agreement.
Partner X cannot retire without the unanimous consent of all creditors.
Retirement is invalid unless approved by the Tribunal.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 24(1) states that a person may cease to be a partner in accordance with agreement with the other partners; hence, the notice period specified in the LLP agreement governs the retirement.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: When does Partner X officially cease to be a partner and get relieved of future partner liabilities?
options: Immediately upon posting the notice
Only when notice of cessation is filed with the Registrar and recorded, or upon expiration of the notice
Only after the financial year audit is completed
When the Tribunal issues a discharge certificate
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 25 mandates that notice of cessation of a partner must be filed with the Registrar within 30 days, and a partner continues to be regarded as a partner until the public notice/filing reflects their cessation, or in accordance with the agreement.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the statutory requirement regarding the preparation and filing of Form 8 (Statement of Account and Solvency) for Vanguard Tech Solutions LLP?
options: It must be filed within 30 days of the end of the financial year.
It must be prepared within 6 months of the end of the financial year and filed in Form 8 within the prescribed due date.
It is optional for LLPs with turnover below Rs. 40 lakhs.
It is filed only once in every five years.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Under Rule 25 and Section 34, every LLP must maintain a Statement of Account and Solvency within 6 months of the end of the financial year and file Form 8 with the Registrar within 30 days of expiration of that 6-month period.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Partner X ceased to be a partner, what is the responsibility for filing the notice of change in partners with the Registrar?
options: Partner X alone is responsible for filing the notice.
The LLP must file the notice of change of partners within 30 days of the cessation.
The Central Government files the notice automatically.
No filing is required if the remaining partners agree.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 25(1) places the obligation on the LLP to file a notice of any change in its partners with the Registrar within 30 days of such change taking place.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: Apex Global Ventures LLP was suspected of carrying on fraudulent transactions to cheat its suppliers. The Central Government ordered an inspection of the LLP's books under Section 43. During the inquiry, Partner M disclosed crucial documents and internal emails proving systemic fraud by the managing designated partner, Mr. K. Partner M sought protection under the whistleblowing provisions of the LLP Act.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Under Section 43, who holds the authority to order an investigation into the affairs of Apex Global Ventures LLP?
options: The High Court of the State
The Central Government
The Reserve Bank of India
The Registrar of Companies independently
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 43 explicitly empowers the Central Government to appoint inspectors to investigate the affairs of an LLP based on specified grounds or reports.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What relief or benefit can Partner M potentially receive under Section 31 for cooperating as a whistleblower?
options: Complete exemption from all civil debts of the LLP
Reduction or waiver of penalty that may be leviable against them
Automatic promotion to the position of managing designated partner
Cash reward equivalent to the fraud amount
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 31 provides that the Tribunal or Central Government may reduce or waive any penalty against a partner or employee who provides useful information leading to a conviction or penalty under the Act.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: If Mr. K is found guilty of carrying on business with intent to defraud creditors under Section 30, what personal liability does he face?
options: Liability limited to his capital contribution only
Unlimited personal liability for all debts of the LLP without any limitation, along with imprisonment and fines
Only a nominal fine of Rs. 1,000
Liability only if the creditors file a civil suit
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 30 makes persons knowingly party to fraudulent trading personally liable, without any limitation, for all or any of the debts or other liabilities of the LLP, in addition to penal imprisonment and fines.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can Apex Global Ventures LLP be wound up by the Tribunal due to fraudulent activities?
options: No, winding up can only be voluntary for LLPs.
Yes, if the Tribunal is of the opinion that it is just and equitable or that the LLP has acted fraudulently, it may order winding up.
Only if 100% of partners consent to Tribunal intervention.
No, fraud only attracts financial penalties, not winding up.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 64 sets out grounds for winding up by the Tribunal, including when the LLP has been used for fraudulent purposes or if the Tribunal thinks it is just and equitable to wind up the LLP.

scenarios.subject: Law
scenarios.passage: GreenFields Agro LLP was established with two corporate bodies as partners: AgriCorp Ltd. and BioInnovations Inc., along with two individual designated partners, Mr. Sharma and Ms. Verma. Due to a severe economic downturn, the LLP incurred heavy trading losses, and its liabilities exceeded its total assets. The partners wish to initiate a voluntary winding up of the LLP.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: What is the primary condition for initiating voluntary winding up of GreenFields Agro LLP under Section 63?
options: Approval from the local municipal corporation
Passing a resolution to wind up voluntarily and complying with the LLP agreement or statutory procedure
Approval from the Supreme Court of India
Full repayment of all creditors prior to passing any resolution
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 63 states that an LLP may be wound up voluntarily if the LLP passes a resolution to wind up voluntarily and follows the prescribed process under the LLP Rules.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Can corporate bodies like AgriCorp Ltd. and BioInnovations Inc. act as partners in GreenFields Agro LLP?
options: No, only living individuals can be partners in an LLP.
Yes, corporate bodies, companies, and foreign LLPs are fully competent to be partners in an LLP.
Yes, but only if they hold more than 50% of the voting power.
No, corporate bodies can only be designated partners, not ordinary partners.
linkedMcqs.explanation: Section 2(1)(d) and Section 5 of the LLP Act permit any individual or body corporate to be a partner in a Limited Liability Partnership.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: During the winding up of GreenFields Agro LLP, what is the extent of liability of AgriCorp Ltd. and BioInnovations Inc. for the shortfall in assets?
options: Unlimited personal liability of both parent companies
Liability limited to their agreed capital contribution to the LLP
No liability whatsoever once winding up is initiated
Joint liability with the designated partners' personal assets
linkedMcqs.explanation: The core feature of an LLP is limited liability. Partners (whether individuals or corporate bodies) are not personally liable for the debts of the LLP beyond their agreed contribution.

linkedMcqs.subject: Law
linkedMcqs.prompt: Who is responsible for overseeing the voluntary winding up process of the LLP once the resolution is passed?
options: The Registrar of Companies directly
A Company Liquidator or liquidator appointed for the LLP in accordance with the rules
The Chief Justice of the High Court
The oldest designated partner automatically
linkedMcqs.explanation: Voluntary winding up procedures under the LLP Act and Rules require the appointment of a liquidator who manages the realization of assets and settlement of claims.
